label: late original-phase input of u/2/q/t/p/z/j/g/e after an i/m/x/d/l/r/a/h prefix
explanation: Fires only during the original (input) phase, at t >= 2. It never fires at t = 0 or 1, on the <DEL> step, or in the copy phase (1 activation in 546k copy steps). Firing rate rises with position: about 3% at orig_idx 2 and about 31% at orig_idx 8. It is highest on the last few tokens before <DEL> (36% of mass at to_go = 0). The current input token matters a lot. u, 2, q and t give the most (rates 16-23%), then p, z, j, g and e. It is mostly first occurrences of the token (88% of mass at in_first = 1). Strength also goes up when the sequence started with, or contains, i, m, x, d, l, r, a or h. The top examples begin with i/d/x and peak on a final u. Adding the condition first_tok in that set raises precision to 0.86 but halves recall. That points to a graded, additive build-up of evidence (position + current token + early-prefix tokens), not a crisp rule. That is why F1 tops out around 0.63. Activations missed by the predicate are weaker, on tokens such as k, c, n, w or 1 late in the sequence. False positives are the listed tokens appearing early or after a prefix with no favourable tokens.
